chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Calling the same top men; first-take dates
summary: Leaders used reliable players like Cozy Cole, and McRae recalls running down keys and introductions and recording first takes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And like a lot of records that you have here -- that's in that book, in all these books -- some of these records we never heard.

Because remember, this was like a side thing. We go in and make a date. You would call and say, "I'm doing a date. I want to get so and so. I'm having so and so, I'm needing so and so." All these different type of outstanding musicians, you know.
Trombone players, trumpet players, guitar players, piano players, drummer. Like you say, Cozy Cole (inaudible) was all around.
Use Cozy, because you know why? Cozy was a good studio drummer. He knew -- good tempo man, you know.
Just like Ron, the bass player. He's just a --
Ron Carter.
Ron Carter. He was -- the other that played with Ella, -- so (inaudible) the other bass player. (inaudible) famous. Great jazz bass player, (inaudible) what's -- Ray?
Ray Brown?

See, we never used to much music. We would just walk in the studio, "Hey, man, what we gonna do?" And Teddy will running it down or whoever be running it down. "Let's run down so and so.
